insider_details.detail: Couples who expect a vows moment should know the Orthodox rite has none (per the Orthodox Church in America): build personal words into the reception speeches rather than asking the priest to add them.

If one partner is not Orthodox, raise it with the parish priest before choosing a church or date: the Orthodox Church in America says the sacrament is for baptised members and allows marriage to a baptised non-Orthodox Christian, so baptism paperwork shapes the timeline.
Brief the photographer and guests that the crowning is the centre of the rite (per the Orthodox Church in America), so the key shots happen at the crowning, not at a ring or vows moment.
